tip.title: Ask one more follow-up question
tip.why: People who ask more questions in a conversation are liked more, and the effect is almost entirely driven by follow-up questions, the ones that pick up what the other person just said. Huang, Yeomans, Brooks, Minson and Gino (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2017) ran three studies of live conversations, including online get-to-know-you chats and face-to-face speed dates. Partners rated high question-askers as more likable, and speed daters who asked more follow-ups were more likely to get a yes to a second date. The mechanism was responsiveness: follow-ups signal that you listened and care. Two cautions from the same work: observers watching from outside did not show the effect, so this is about the person in front of you, and rapid-fire or off-topic questions can backfire. People also badly underpredict how much asking helps, which is why most of us switch topics instead.
how: In your next conversation today, when someone finishes a thought, ask one question about what they just said before you add anything of your own.
Make it a real follow-up ('what did you do when that happened?'), not a topic switch or a mirror question ('and you?').
Aim for one extra follow-up per conversation, not an interrogation; the study's warning is that too many, or the wrong kind, hurts.
tip.src: Huang et al. · J Pers Soc Psychol, 2017
tip.ask: Which conversation today got better after one more follow-up question, and what did you learn that you would otherwise have missed?

markets.headline: Stocks slipped a fifth straight day Wednesday as the Fed's minutes pointed to more hikes and Nvidia reversed lower; the S&P 500 lost 0.2% to 7,323.63, and Anthropic priced a record IPO at $83 after the close.
points: The S&P 500 fell 16.90 points (0.23%) to 7,323.63, its fifth straight loss and longest losing run since June, and closed below its 200-day moving average. The Dow dropped about 561 points (1.1%) to 50,198.17, led by a 10.2% slide in UnitedHealth after a CMS proposal to extrapolate Medicare Advantage audit findings, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42% to 24,429.88. The 2 PM ET release of the Fed's October minutes, which showed almost all officials expecting more hikes and a couple open to a half-point move in December, took the air out of a morning rally. Nvidia reversed an early gain to close down 2.89% at $150.96 despite Tuesday's $115.8 billion quarter and $130 billion guide, as questions about who follows Jensen Huang outweighed the numbers; AMD (+5.31%) and Broadcom (+3.64%) rose on the read-through. Retail earnings were the bright spot: TJX gained 8.05% on a 4% comp, Target rose 4.01% on EPS of $2.65 versus $2.07 expected (about $0.50 from tariff refunds), and Lowe's added 1.05%. After the bell, Palo Alto Networks rose on a beat, and Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, above the $70 to $78 range, selling about 980 million shares to raise $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record; it starts trading Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT.

Tesla rose $3.61 (0.95%) to $383.72, outperforming the index for a second day without a single catalyst. The news flow was Musk's DealBook remarks that Tesla and SpaceX are 'probably' better together and that he should not get Tesla pay awards for a merger, the opening of Cybercab orders at $29,990, Monday's roughly $3.3 billion Giga Berlin expansion that Tesla says could eventually build up to 1 million Cybercabs a year, and a Cybercab teaser for Dallas. The stock remains about 15% below its 2025 close of $449.81.

Intel slipped $0.50 (0.91%) to $54.67, a third straight decline after Monday's 7% drop and Tuesday's small loss, trading between $53.44 and $56.00. The slide came even as Intel and Microsoft announced an expanded Azure infrastructure partnership; weighing on the stock were Nvidia's 13F showing it cut its Intel stake by about a quarter and the proposed shareholder class action filed in federal court in San Jose over the Q4 forecast. Intel is still up about 48% for 2026 from its $36.90 close on Dec. 31, 2025.

SpaceX gained $1.80 (1.27%) to $143.50, its second straight advance after Tuesday's 3.2% rise on the CFO's AI remarks. Musk told DealBook that Anthropic is 'extremely likely' to add about 10 gigawatts of SpaceX compute on top of the Colossus 1 capacity it already rents, though Anthropic has not confirmed that; nearby items were a Texas air permit for a planned SpaceX data center and a large holder's filing. The stock sits about 6% above its $135 June IPO price and about 36% below its $225.64 52-week high; the Dec. 8 insider lock-up expiry is the next date traders are watching.

pick.name: Sandisk
pick.theme: AI memory: a NAND maker down 60% from its June peak, splitting 8-for-1 on Friday
pick.what: Sandisk designs and sells NAND flash memory and storage products: enterprise SSDs for data centers, client SSDs for PCs, embedded flash for phones and cars, and consumer cards and drives. It was spun out of Western Digital in February 2025 and trades on Nasdaq as SNDK, with manufacturing through a long-running joint venture with Japan's Kioxia. In 2026 the stock became one of the main ways to play the AI-driven shortage in memory chips, as hyperscalers bought flash to feed inference workloads.
pick.why: Three things make it worth a look right now. First, the stock completes an eight-for-one split after Thursday's close, so from Friday the quote drops from about $776 to roughly $97, and split days often bring a burst of attention and volume. Second, it has been crushed: after rising to a $2,354.39 high on June 22, SNDK fell 2.64% to $776.22 on Nov 18, down about 32% in November alone and roughly 62% from the peak, even though it is still up about 270% for 2026. The November damage came from a 22% one-day drop on Nov 5 in the chip selloff, Kioxia's warning that the AI-driven jump in flash prices is fading, a GF Securities note on possible 2027 oversupply, and the disclosure that Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne sold its whole position. Third, the fundamentals reported so far have not broken: fiscal Q1 revenue was $11.03 billion against a $10.70 billion consensus with adjusted EPS of $49.51 versus $46.36, and Nvidia's $130 billion Q4 guide this week argues AI data-center buildouts are not slowing. Analysts have not given up either: Benzinga's tally (as of Nov 5) shows 17 of 18 rating it Buy with one Hold, and an average target of $1,636.83, more than double the current price. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: Memory is the most cyclical corner of semiconductors, and the stock is already behaving like the cycle has turned: Kioxia, Sandisk's own manufacturing partner, guided below estimates and said flash price gains are fading, and at least one broker sees oversupply in 2027. Daily moves of 10% to 20% in either direction have been common this fall, Fox Advisors downgraded the shares on Nov 2, and the analyst targets are from early November and may be cut. The split changes nothing about the business, pre-split and post-split prices will be confusing for a few days, and a stock that fell 62% can keep falling if NAND contract prices roll over.

btc.summary: Cowen's newest upload, a 48-minute video posted Wednesday morning and titled Bitcoin: The Bull's Dilemma, argues that the bullish case has gotten harder to make from the data. Working from his chapter list, he starts with stablecoins: the total stablecoin market cap has broken support and Tether's share of the crypto market keeps rising, which in his framework means money is parked rather than deployed, and he ties that to a stronger dollar, tightening liquidity and the same rate-hike pressure that is weighing on equities. He then leans on history, noting that gold has tended to bottom before bitcoin in past cycles and comparing the 2008 gold-versus-stocks episode, and he walks through the midterm-year path, a possible December government shutdown and the FOMC calendar as the near-term event risks. The on-chain section is the heart of the dilemma: metrics like the MVRV Z-score have not reset to the levels that marked earlier cycle lows, so he lays out scenarios from bitcoin holding its recent floor to lower lows, with his balance-price model marking a much deeper bear case. His stance is unchanged: stay open-minded about the downside, keep averaging in rather than calling the bottom, and watch the stock market, since in his view bitcoin's final low of this cycle follows the second real equity correction rather than leading it.

brief.lede: Hyundai buys the rest of Boston Dynamics and sets a 30,000-Atlas target while Musk promises an unedited Optimus video within two months; Anthropic prices the largest IPO on record at $83, Google ships Gemini 4 Neon, the Fed's minutes point to more rate hikes, Musk calls a Tesla-SpaceX merger 'probably' right, and bitcoin ETFs post their worst day of the week.

articles.title: Hyundai takes all of Boston Dynamics and targets 30,000 Atlas a year
body: Hyundai Motor Group now owns Boston Dynamics outright after paying SoftBank about **$325 million** for the remaining 9.65% stake, the Korea Herald and Seoul's Financial News reported on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The buyout ends the 2021 arrangement in which SoftBank kept a minority slice after selling control to Hyundai, and it puts the Atlas humanoid fully inside the carmaker's manufacturing plans.

Those plans are large. The group says it wants annual production capacity of around **30,000 Atlas robots by 2028**, with the first deployment at Hyundai's plant in Georgia, where the robots would start on lower-intensity work such as sorting and carrying parts between stations. One report said advisers are weighing an IPO around 2029 or 2030; nothing has been filed, and no customer pricing has been published.

The financials show why Hyundai wanted full control rather than a shared board. For January through September, Boston Dynamics' revenue rose 29% to about 136 billion won, which is under $100 million at recent exchange rates, while its net loss widened to about 626.6 billion won, roughly four and a half times revenue. The third quarter alone lost 237.8 billion won on 54.7 billion won of sales. That is the cost of standing up production, and a bill only a parent like Hyundai pays willingly. Tuesday's GlobalFoundries fab trial is the first non-automotive customer in that pipeline.

Tesla's Optimus, the other carmaker humanoid, has a date of sorts. In an interview reported on Wednesday, Nov. 18, Elon Musk said Tesla intends to release unedited footage of Optimus doing real tasks within about **two months**, repeating a promise from the October earnings call that the demo would not be canned, with no teleoperation and no pre-programmed routines. Several outlets say the third-generation robot is slated for an on-site demonstration at the Humanoids Summit in San Mateo on Dec. 1 and 2, which falls inside that window; Tesla has not confirmed a venue.

Elsewhere, ROBOTERA said in a Nov. 19 release that its M7 humanoid sorted parcels live at the APEC CEO Summit, held Nov. 17 to 19. And a deals tracker dated Nov. 16 listed a $300 million Series E for Path Robotics, the Columbus, Ohio maker of AI welding robots, at a $2.45 billion valuation led by Georgian; the figure comes from the tracker, not a company release, so treat it as unconfirmed.

What it means: the field now has two carmakers that own their humanoid programs outright and will carry heavy losses toward a production target three years out. Hyundai's 30,000-a-year figure and Musk's two-month video promise are both claims to check against deliveries, but they set the bar that every startup raising money this month will be measured against.

articles.title: Anthropic prices at $83 and raises a record $81 billion
body: Anthropic priced its initial public offering on Wednesday evening at **$83.00 a share**, above the $70 to $78 range it marketed on the roadshow, and enlarged the deal to **980 million Class A shares** from 825 million, the company said in a short notice on its site. Anthropic itself is selling about 956.4 million shares and existing holders about 23.6 million; the company gets nothing from the holders' portion. Trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT is expected to begin today, Thursday, Nov. 19, with the offering set to close Friday.

At $83 the base deal grosses about $81.3 billion, of which roughly $79.4 billion goes to Anthropic before fees. CNBC called it the largest IPO on record by proceeds, ahead of SpaceX's $75 billion listing in June. Underwriters led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley also hold a 30-day option on up to 147 million more shares, worth another $12.2 billion at the offer price. Those figures are arithmetic from the company's notice, which does not state proceeds or an implied valuation.

The price is 6.4% above the top of the range and about 12% above the midpoint, and the share count grew by nearly 19%, both signs of a book that was reported as several times covered in the days before pricing. Press estimates of the valuation differ with the share count used: TechCrunch and others put the common-stock market value near **$1.1 trillion**, and the fully diluted figure around $1.5 trillion, well above the $965 billion private mark set in May. Anthropic has not published a market capitalization.

The separate roughly $26 billion Class N private placement by strategic holders including Google and Nvidia, disclosed with the roadshow, runs alongside the public deal. Nasdaq's first trade is set by its opening auction and can print well after the 9:30 AM Eastern bell, so an opening price may not exist until midmorning Pacific.

What to watch: the first print relative to $83, whether the greenshoe is exercised, and how a listed frontier lab trades against Nvidia, which has lost roughly a third of its value since October. This is also the first time a company whose main product is a large language model carries a daily public price, which gives every other lab's private valuation a live benchmark.

articles.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Neon as Chinese labs blunt hacking skills
body: Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Neon worldwide on Wednesday, Nov. 18, a model built for long-running agent work and especially coding. API pricing is **$3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens**, with cached inputs at $0.15, a 1-million-token context window and four thinking levels from Low to Extra High. It is rolling out to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app and to developers through the paid Gemini API, AI Studio and Android Studio; the weights are closed.

Google's own numbers put Neon first on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index at **58.6**, at 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, and at 61 on the broader Intelligence Index at the Extra High setting, third overall at launch. Two caveats travel with those figures: the coding score was produced with Google's Antigravity command-line harness, and at least one outlet noted that Neon still trails Claude Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and FrontierCode 2.0. Google also says Neon's default High setting costs 32% less per task than Carbon on its comparison set.

Neon is Google's fourth new Gemini model in seven weeks, after Carbon and Hydrogen earlier this month. The pattern is a frontier model followed quickly by cheaper, narrower tiers, which is the same shape OpenAI used with GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on Tuesday and Microsoft with its MAI line at Ignite.

The other model story this week comes from China. Bloomberg reported on Nov. 16, with Digitimes and Business Standard following on Nov. 17, that Alibaba, Tencent and Moonshot AI have deliberately limited the offensive cyber abilities of their newest models. Alibaba's Qwen4-Max was trained on data filtered to keep defensive security knowledge and drop material that would help attacks, and its secure-code generation score reportedly rose to 14.7% from 8%; Tencent says cyber training for its Hy4 model is restricted to defense; Moonshot trimmed attack capabilities from Kimi K3.1 Pro; and Zhipu plans to put its most sensitive capabilities behind a verification wall. Reports differ on whether Qwen4-Max shipped with open weights.

The moves line up with a draft Chinese rule that would ban exports of tools aimed at critical infrastructure and could restrict overseas deployment of models deemed world-leading. It is the mirror image of OpenAI's gated GPT-6 Cyber release two weeks ago: both sides are now treating offensive cyber skill as a controlled capability rather than a benchmark to win.

What it means: for anyone building agents, the practical news is a third strong coding model at mid-tier prices, which keeps pushing the cost of long agent runs down. The policy news is that capability restraint on cyber has gone from an American lab practice to something China's largest labs do under their own government's pressure, which narrows the range of what any open-weight release will contain.

articles.title: Fed minutes point to more hikes as Palo Alto and the retailers beat
body: The minutes of the Fed's October meeting, released Wednesday at 2 PM Eastern, show a committee that is done debating whether to tighten and is now arguing about how fast. Officials held the policy rate at 3.75% to 4% by a **10 to 2 vote**, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike, and the minutes say almost all participants judged further increases likely to be appropriate. A couple were open to a December move larger than a quarter point if the data disappoint, and the minutes flagged the AI buildout as both an inflation and a financial-stability risk.

Governor Christopher Waller went further the same day, saying the Fed may need to shock markets with a half-point hike in December. Rate futures, per Bloomberg, now price quarter-point increases in December and January and another by April. Stocks gave back a morning rally after the release: the S&P 500 slipped 0.23% to 7,323.63, a **fifth straight loss** and its longest run since June, the Dow fell 1.1% on a 10% drop in UnitedHealth, and the Nasdaq rose 0.4%. Nvidia reversed an early gain to close down 2.9% despite Tuesday's beat.

The Nvidia story has moved from numbers to governance. Jensen Huang said on Tuesday he would be honored to return if the board thought it best; chair Harvey Jones replied on the earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him. Interim chief Colette Kress said demand for the Vera Rubin platform is off to an explosive start. Newsquawk reported that Huang will appear before House panels on Dec. 1.

Palo Alto Networks reported after the close. Revenue grew 39% to **$3.44 billion** and next-generation security annual recurring revenue, the subscription run rate for its newer cloud and AI products, rose 66% to $9.73 billion; non-GAAP earnings were $1.05 a share against guidance of $0.96 to $0.98, while GAAP operating income fell to $96 million from $309 million a year earlier. Contracted backlog grew 35% to $21 billion, and the company said it intends to buy Applied Compute, a platform for post-training and running open-weight models, and CNBC said the shares rose in extended trading.

Retail earnings were the morning's bright spot: TJX gained 8% on a 4% comp against a 2% to 3% guide, Target rose 4% on a 5.6% comp and earnings of $2.65 a share, about 50 cents of it from tariff refunds, and Lowe's, whose $3.10 also leaned on refunds, closed up about 1% after a weak premarket.

What it means: the market is now pricing three more hikes into a tape where AI infrastructure demand looks intact at Nvidia and Palo Alto and the consumer looks fine at TJX and Target. With Anthropic's debut today adding a third large AI name to the screen, the next few sessions are a direct test of how much of that demand investors will pay for at higher rates.

articles.title: Musk says Tesla and SpaceX are 'probably' better together
body: Elon Musk told the New York Times DealBook Summit by video on Wednesday, Nov. 18 that Tesla and SpaceX have grown more overlapping, especially in AI and robotics, and answered **"probably yes"** when Andrew Ross Sorkin asked whether the two companies would be better together. He said the decision rests with shareholders and a Tesla vote may or may not succeed, and he added that he should not receive his Tesla stock awards simply for a merger, since they were meant to reward Tesla performance. Both companies have formed committees of independent directors; no terms have been announced.

He also sketched the next robotaxi: a Model Y variant with no steering wheel or pedals, built to carry six or seven people. That follows Tesla's Nov. 16 confirmation of a first-phase investment of about 3 billion euros, roughly **$3.3 billion**, in a new building at Giga Berlin designed for up to 1 million Cybercabs a year, with production planned for 2029; Electrek noted that EU rules currently cap driverless cars at 1,500 per model, which makes the ceiling a long-term number. A permit filing is due by year-end and construction in the first half of 2027, per one report.

On the SpaceX side, Musk said Anthropic is extremely likely to add roughly **10 gigawatts** of compute from SpaceX, which already rents Anthropic the whole of its Colossus 1 site in Memphis. He described the arrangements as short-term contracts either side can end on a few months' notice and called power, not chips, the limiting factor. Anthropic has not confirmed the 10-gigawatt figure, and one analysis stressed that it is interest, not a signed contract. SpaceX shares rose 1.3% to $143.50.

Cybercab itself keeps inching outward. Tesla posted a teaser of Cybercab rides in Dallas with the caption "Just leaving this here," which Drive Tesla read as an imminent launch; Texas registrations now show 773 Cybercabs in a fleet of more than 1,500 Robotaxis. Bloomberg Opinion argued the $29,990 car is really built for fleets, since owners cannot resell it or earn money with it without Tesla's permission.

Two Electrek items round out the week. Tesla is tightening FSD driver monitoring in Europe, with earlier warnings, a strike for looking away during a maneuver and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h, while recent US builds nag less and Musk has told owners they can text. And the Semi charging network stands at 7 sites against a goal of 37 for 2026, with six weeks left.

What it means: the merger talk is now coming from Musk himself rather than from Bloomberg's sources, and the Berlin plan commits real money to Cybercab as a global product, not a Texas pilot. Watch for the Dallas launch date, any Anthropic confirmation of the 10-gigawatt figure, and whether the Dec. 3 shareholder meeting adds a merger item.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose $306 million as the minutes revive hike fears
body: US spot bitcoin ETFs saw a net outflow of about **$306.5 million** on Wednesday, Nov. 18, according to Farside and SoSoValue data relayed by several crypto outlets, and none of the twelve funds took in money. BlackRock's IBIT led with roughly $149 million out and Fidelity's FBTC about $69 million; Ethereum funds lost another $39.8 million. The week's first three sessions add up to about $538 million of withdrawals, and November's total is approaching $2.9 billion.

The price followed the Fed. Bitcoin held near $64,600 into the afternoon, then dropped close to 3% to about **$62,500** after the October minutes showed almost all officials expecting more hikes, with a couple open to a half-point move in December. Futures now put December hike odds near 90%, the crypto Fear and Greed index sits at 11, deep in extreme fear, and bitcoin trades roughly 26% below its October high.

Benjamin Cowen's Wednesday video, titled The Bull's Dilemma, lays out why he thinks the bulls' case has gotten harder. His chapter list runs through stablecoin market cap breaking support and rising Tether dominance, both signs of money waiting on the sidelines; the historical pattern of gold bottoming before bitcoin; the fact that on-chain metrics such as the MVRV Z-score have not reset to prior cycle lows; a December government shutdown as event risk; and a scenario analysis that ranges from bitcoin holding its recent floor to his balance-price model, which points much lower.

The institutional side has its own calendar. Senate Banking hears from the SEC nominees today, the CLARITY market-structure bill remains parked until January, and Strategy's weekly filing on Monday showed it still buying in small size. None of that changes the near-term driver, which is a Fed moving the other way from every rate cut the 2024 and 2025 rally was built on.

What it means: three straight days of outflows into a hawkish Fed is the pattern that has preceded each leg down this autumn. Cowen's framework says the low arrives only after equities take a second real correction, and the S&P 500 has now closed below its 200-day average, so the two markets he watches are finally moving together.

items.where: Rancho San Antonio Open Space Preserve, Cupertino / Los Altos
items.blurb: Sunday, Nov 22, morning. Free, open from dawn to a half hour after sunset. Midweek rain means the dirt sections will be slick; stick to the wider fire roads if showers continue into the weekend.

cal.tips: About 15 minutes from Mountain View via Foothill Expressway to Cristo Rey Drive; the lots fill by 9 AM on weekends and parking on Cristo Rey itself is ticketed, so arrive early or go after 2 PM. items.title: Great Dickens Christmas Fair opening weekend
items.blurb: Saturday, Nov 21 and Sunday, Nov 22, 10 AM to 6 PM, the first of five weekends running through Dec 20 plus the Friday after Thanksgiving. The Cow Palace's exhibition halls become a lamplit Victorian London with hundreds of costumed performers, pubs, dance halls, music halls and shops, and the only stage version of A Christmas Carol you can wander through. Tickets are date-specific and sold only through dickensfair.com; general admission is listed at about $35, with parking $20 per car. Opening day is the busiest, so Sunday is the calmer choice.

cal.location: Cow Palace, 2600 Geneva Ave, Daly City, CA 94014
cal.tips: About 40-50 minutes from Mountain View on US-101 north to the Cow Palace exit at Geneva Avenue; parking is $20, card or cash, and the lot is slow to clear at closing. Transit is awkward (Caltrain to San Francisco then Muni 8 or 9 to Geneva), so driving or a rideshare is simpler. Dress in layers since the halls are drafty, budget for food and drink inside, and arrive near 10 AM to see the opening procession.

vocab.def: The warmth of the sun in winter; the feeling of sunshine on a cold day. A rare, nearly obsolete word first recorded in English in 1623.

cards.b: From Latin apricus, 'warmed by the sun, sunny' (apricari, 'to bask in the sun'); the same root gives 'apricot' by way of a folk etymology
winter sunshine, sun-warmth; no exact single-word synonym, which is why people keep reviving it. Opposite idea: chill, rawness
the first clear afternoon after a storm, a cold morning on a sunny bench, the patch of sun a cat finds in December

examples: After two days of rain the clouds broke around three, and the whole office drifted outside for ten minutes of apricity.
The trail was still muddy, but the apricity on the ridge made the climb feel like a reward.
vocab.ex: After two days of rain the clouds broke around three, and the whole office drifted outside for ten minutes of apricity.

vocab.def: Of or relating to rain; marked by heavy or abundant rainfall. In geology, a pluvial is a long wet period in a region's climate history.

cards.b: From Latin pluvia, 'rain' (pluere, 'to rain'); the same root gives Spanish lluvia and French pluie
rainy, wet, sodden; the technical cousin of 'drizzly' and 'monsoonal'. Antonym: arid
a storm day like this one, a wet winter, a region's rainy season, or a lake that filled during an ancient wet epoch

examples: The whole Peninsula went pluvial overnight: creeks up, lights out, the bike lane a river.
Lake Lahontan is a ghost of the last pluvial, when Nevada was wet enough to hold an inland sea.
vocab.ex: The whole Peninsula went pluvial overnight: creeks up, lights out, the bike lane a river.

vocab.def: A clumsy, inelegant fix that works anyway: a solution bolted together from mismatched parts because it had to ship today.

cards.b: Engineering slang popularized by Jackson Granholm's 1962 Datamation essay 'How to Design a Kludge'; often traced to German klug ('clever') or Scots cludgie, though the origin is disputed
hack, workaround, bodge, duct-tape fix, Rube Goldberg machine; the opposite of an elegant design
a zip-tied cable harness that shipped, the regex that parses a log file nobody will ever touch again, a hotfix with a TODO from 2023 still in it

examples: The gripper timing was a kludge, a 40-millisecond sleep nobody could explain, and it held through the whole demo.
Every lab has one kludge it is secretly proud of, and it is usually load-bearing.
vocab.ex: The gripper timing was a kludge, a 40-millisecond sleep nobody could explain, and it held through the whole demo.

vocab.def: Studied carelessness: the art of making something difficult look effortless, hiding all the work that went into it.

cards.b: Italian, coined by Baldassare Castiglione in The Book of the Courtier (1528) for the grace of a courtier who never seems to be trying
nonchalance, effortless grace, understated mastery; the opposite of visible strain or showing your work
a demo that looks easy because of three weeks of tuning, a chef plating without looking, an open-collar suit that took an hour

examples: The demo had real sprezzatura: the robot folded the shirt like an afterthought, and nobody saw the 400 failed runs behind it.
His slides have a kind of sprezzatura, four words a page and not a hint of the late nights that produced them.
vocab.ex: The demo had real sprezzatura: the robot folded the shirt like an afterthought, and nobody saw the 400 failed runs behind it.

vocab.def: A manuscript page that was scraped clean and written over, with traces of the old text still showing; by extension, anything that carries visible layers of its earlier versions.

cards.b: Greek palin ('again') + psēstos ('scraped'): parchment was expensive, so monks scraped off old texts and reused the skin
layered record, overwritten text, accretion; near relatives: patina, sediment, legacy code
a city block with 1920s brick behind a glass facade, a codebase where every refactor left fossils, a face that shows every earlier age

examples: The robot's control stack is a palimpsest: PID loops from 2019 still run under three generations of learned policies.
Downtown is a palimpsest of booms, with the cannery brick, the dot-com stucco and the new glass all on one block.
vocab.ex: The robot's control stack is a palimpsest: PID loops from 2019 still run under three generations of learned policies.

vocab.def: Relating to or living on the banks of a river or stream; the strip of land, plants and animals that depend on a waterway.

cards.b: Latin ripa ('riverbank'), the same root as the Spanish ribera and the French rive
riverside, streamside, bankside, littoral (for a lake or sea)
the willows along Stevens Creek, a wildlife corridor, the law of who owns a riverbank

examples: The riparian corridor along the creek was the only green line left on the map by August.
Water rights here are riparian: if your land touches the stream, you get a share of it.
vocab.ex: The riparian corridor along the creek was the only green line left on the map by August.

vocab.def: Glowing or flickering softly over a surface; of wit or light, playing lightly and brilliantly without heat.

cards.b: Latin lambere ('to lick'): a flame that licks across a surface without burning it
glowing, flickering, luminous, softly radiant
late sun on the bay, a gas flame on a stove, a friend's light and quick humor

examples: By 4:30 the lambent light off the salt ponds made even the parking lot look painted.
Her lambent wit kept the review going for two hours without anyone noticing the time.
vocab.ex: By 4:30 the lambent light off the salt ponds made even the parking lot look painted.

spanish.meaning: Almost; just about; any minute now
spanish.note: Mero is a Mexican all-purpose intensifier, and ya mero is how you say something is almost done, almost here or almost true. Ya mero llego means I'm almost there, which in practice can mean anywhere from two minutes to twenty. Said with a rising tone and a question mark, ¿ya mero? means 'almost done?' or 'are we there yet?'. It is friendlier and vaguer than casi, which makes it the natural answer when someone asks how much longer.

cards.es: Ya mero llego, pide las chelas
cards.en: I'm almost there, order the beers
Are you almost done?

cards.es: Ya mero se me cae el teléfono
cards.en: My phone is about to die (literally: about to fall)

parts.en: already, now (here: a marker of 'at this point')
very, right, exact; Mexican intensifier (el mero mero is 'the big boss')
right now, soon-ish; the cousin that means anything from now to never

dialog.es: ¿Y la pizza? Ya tengo hambre.
dialog.en: And the pizza? I'm hungry already.

dialog.en: It's almost here, they said twenty minutes.

dialog.es: Eso dijeron hace media hora.
dialog.en: They said that half an hour ago.

dialog.es: Ya mero, ya mero. Ten paciencia.
dialog.en: Almost, almost. Be patient.

spanish.use: Text it when you're five minutes out from meeting someone; it sounds relaxed and local, and it buys you a little slack.

spanish.note: Agüitarse is pure Mexican slang for getting sad, discouraged or deflated, and no te agüites is how a friend tells you to shake it off. It is softer than 'cheer up' and warmer than 'don't worry': it names the slump and waves it away in one breath. You hear it after a bad day at work, a cancelled plan or a rained-out weekend. The adjective form is agüitado: ando bien agüitado means I'm feeling pretty down.

cards.es: No te agüites, mañana lo arreglamos
cards.en: Don't get bummed, we'll fix it tomorrow

cards.es: Ando medio agüitado por la lluvia

to get down, to deflate; Mexican slang
come on, go on (often follows it: 'no te agüites, ándale')

dialog.es: Es que ya tenía todo listo.
dialog.en: It's just that I already had everything ready.

dialog.es: Ya sé. Hoy te invito unos tacos y listo.
dialog.en: I know. Tonight the tacos are on me and that's that.

spanish.use: Say it to a coworker whose plans got rained out today; it lands as warm and local, not as advice.

spanish.phrase: Me voy a echar un coyotito
spanish.pron: meh voy ah eh-CHAR oon ko-yo-TEE-toh
spanish.meaning: I'm going to take a quick nap
spanish.note: Literally 'I'm going to throw myself a little coyote'. In Mexico, echarse un coyotito is the everyday way to say you are grabbing a short nap, usually after lunch or before going out. Warm and a bit playful, fine with coworkers and family alike, and it makes the nap sound like a plan instead of a lapse. The reflexive echarse ('to throw oneself') shows up all over casual Mexican Spanish for doing something quickly: echarse un taco, echarse una pestañita.

cards.es: Me voy a echar un coyotito, ¿me despiertas en veinte?
cards.en: I'm going to take a quick nap, wake me in twenty?

cards.es: Me eché una pestañita en el tren
cards.en: I dozed off for a bit on the train (literally 'a little eyelash')

cards.es: Ando que me caigo de sueño
cards.en: I'm so tired I could fall over

parts.en: I'm off, I'm going (irse, to leave)
to throw; here 'to have' or 'to take', as in echarse algo
little coyote (diminutive of coyote), slang for a short nap

dialog.es: ¿Vienes al café o qué?
dialog.en: Are you coming for coffee or what?

dialog.es: Dame veinte minutos, me voy a echar un coyotito.
dialog.en: Give me twenty minutes, I'm going to take a quick nap.

dialog.es: ¿Otra vez? Anoche no dormiste, ¿verdad?
dialog.en: Again? You didn't sleep last night, did you?

dialog.es: Casi nada. Al rato te alcanzo.
dialog.en: Barely. I'll catch up with you in a bit.

spanish.use: Say it after lunch today when you feel yourself fading; it names the nap, gets a smile, and nobody argues with a coyotito.

I'm going to walk the dog

spanish.meaning: I spaced out / I lost my train of thought
spanish.note: Literally 'the plane left on me'. In Mexico it is the standard way to say your mind wandered off: you missed what someone said, forgot what you were about to say, or drove past your exit. Friendly and self-deprecating, fine with anyone, and the perfect thing to say in a meeting when someone has to repeat the question.

cards.es: Perdón, se me fue el avión, ¿qué decías?
cards.en: Sorry, I spaced out, what were you saying?
Same idea: I lost the thread
I've got my head in the clouds today

to me (the one it happened to)
to zone out, lose your train of thought

dialog.es: Que si movemos la prueba al jueves.
dialog.en: Whether we move the test to Thursday.

dialog.es: Ah, sí, el jueves está perfecto.
dialog.en: Oh, yes, Thursday is perfect.

spanish.use: Say it the moment you realize you missed the last 30 seconds of a conversation today; it gets a laugh and a repeat, not an eye-roll.

spanish.meaning: It just clicked / now I get it
spanish.note: Literally 'the twenty just dropped on me'. Old Mexican payphones took a 20-centavo coin, and the call connected only when the coin dropped. So 'me cayó el veinte' is the moment the line goes live in your head: you finally understand something that had been sitting in front of you. Everyday, friendly, safe with anyone.

cards.en: Has it clicked for you yet?

cards.es: Hasta ahora me cae el veinte

spanish.meaning: What a drag / I really can't be bothered
spanish.note: Hueva is literally fish roe, but in Mexico it means laziness or boredom. '¡Qué hueva!' is the groan you let out when something tedious lands on you: a rainy Sunday errand, a long meeting, a form. Among friends only; it is mildly crude, so skip it with your boss or your partner's parents.

dare.title: Climb a wall for the first time
dare.why: The rain clears out this afternoon and the evening is yours, so spend it doing something your body has never done. After work drive ten minutes to Movement Sunnyvale on Stewart Drive, buy a day pass (about $35, rental shoes a few dollars more; weekday hours run late, so you have time), skip the ropes entirely and head for the bouldering walls, the short ones with thick mats and no harness. Start on the easiest color and work up for an hour. The one rule that makes it count: pick a problem that looks a little too hard for you, fall off it at least three times, then ask whoever is nearby how they did the move.
dare.worth: Bouldering is the rare sport where night one already feels like progress: you can see the top, you either get there or you don't, and strangers at the wall will coach you without being asked. You will drive home with sore forearms and a new way to spend a rainy evening.

swap.title: Catch the post-storm sunset
swap.why: Sunset is about 4:55 PM. Fifteen minutes before, step outside wherever you are, find the clearest line of sight west, and watch the storm-washed sky do its thing until the light goes. Phone stays in your pocket; the first day after a front passes usually has the best color of the month.
swap.worth: You live under some of the best post-storm skies in the country and almost never stop for them. This is the cheapest ten minutes of awe available today.
